function_question: How does nature keep fins and wings working at steep angles?

opening.text: There was a boy called Arman, 15, who spent every lunch break in the school workshop building things that move.
Arman tuned the little wind turbine he was building for the school science and engineering fair, counting its turns in the breeze.
At the outdoor test, a gust hit and the turbine slowed to a stop. "It stalls just when the wind gets interesting," Arman groaned. "The fair is in two weeks."

card.place: A school science and engineering fair
card.problem: The turbine stalls in gusty wind
card.goal: Prove a blade edge that works at steep angles
card.rules: A fair test with a control and 3 trials

guide.brief: I'm Popi, your story guide. Arman's wind turbine stalls every time a gust hits, and the science fair is in two weeks. Can you help him? Let's start!
guide.your_idea: Some engineers already have a hunch about gusty wind. Do you?
guide.nature_clues: Nature solved stalling long before engineers named it. Tap each card to meet four heroes of steep angles!
guide.design_secret: Here's the trick the humpback whale knows…
guide.skill: A result only counts if the test is fair. Which pinwheel edge will spin most at a steep angle? Predict first, then count the turns.
guide.sketch: Draw your blade from above and from the side, and write your hypothesis like a real scientist.
guide.build_and_test: Test your smooth control and your bumpy blade at a steep angle, 3 trials each. What are the averages?
guide.retry_tip: Change ONE variable, like bump size or spacing, and test it against the same control. That's how real engineers learn.
guide.ending: And ever since then, Arman's turbine keeps spinning through the gusts, and his notebook is full of whale-inspired blade ideas!

quick_check.question: Arman's rotor makes 36 full turns in 10 seconds. How many turns is that per minute (rpm)?
quick_check.right: Right! A minute has 6 lots of 10 seconds, so 36 × 6 = 216 rpm.
quick_check.wrong: Not quite. A minute is 60 seconds, which is 6 lots of 10 seconds.

clue_cards.name: Humpback whale
clue_cards.trick: Big bumps called tubercles line the front edge of its flippers.
clue_cards.does: They split the water into channels, so the flipper keeps working at angles about 40% steeper.

clue_cards.name: Owl
clue_cards.trick: Its front wing feathers have a jagged, comb-like edge.
clue_cards.does: The comb breaks the air into tiny swirls, so its flight is almost silent.

clue_cards.name: Maple seed
clue_cards.trick: A swirl of air stays stuck along its wing's front edge as it spins.
clue_cards.does: The swirl gives extra lift, so the seed falls slowly and drifts far.

clue_cards.name: Dragonfly
clue_cards.trick: Its thin wings are pleated like a paper fan.
clue_cards.does: Tiny swirls sit in the grooves and help the wing grip the air at steep angles.

predict.prompt: Does the air stay attached, or does the wing stall? Predict first!

items.label: A smooth wing tilted gently, at about 5°
A smooth wing tilted very steeply, at about 25°
A bumpy-edged flipper at a steep angle

predict.explain: At gentle angles, air follows the whole wing. Tilt a smooth wing too far and the air breaks away from the top, so the lift collapses: that's a stall. Bumps on the front edge help the air stay attached at steeper angles.

lab.title: The leading-edge lab
lab.predict: Four pinwheels face the same fan at the same steep angle. Which leading edge will make the most turns in 10 seconds?

tool.name: Biomimicry Design Spiral
tool.intro: You already know Define, Biologize and Discover. Today you'll learn the last 3 steps of the Design Spiral: Abstract, Emulate and Evaluate. Then you loop round again!

parts.name: Abstract
parts.what: Turn nature's strategy into a design principle, in plain words, without the living thing.
parts.example: ☂️ "A surface that bends along flexible lines lets strong wind pass instead of breaking it."
parts.starter: Without the whale, the principle is: a front edge with…

parts.name: Emulate
parts.what: Use that principle in your own design.
parts.example: ☂️ An umbrella with flexible vents that open in a gust, then close again.
parts.starter: On my blade, I will copy the principle by…

parts.name: Evaluate
parts.what: Test it fairly, then check it against nature: does it work, and is it simple and made from little material?
parts.example: ☂️ Test 3 umbrellas in the same fan wind and count the flips. Which one is lightest too?
parts.starter: My fair test compares… and keeps the same…

sketch_checklist: I drew my blade from above and from the side.
I labelled the leading edge, blade angle and bump spacing.
I wrote my hypothesis: If…, then…, because…

test.measure: pinwheel turns in 10 s at a steep angle
test.check_question: Fair test check: how close were your 3 trials to each other?

reflection.question: Which nature trick helped your blade the most?
